summary: Final unchanged position as the run's budget expires (validated: no_change, no new records, no execution requested). Three sourced findings stand, each with receipts and recorded limits. (1) omnipaxos_runtime's unconsumed bounded event stream parks the actor loop — no ticks, no incoming handling, no command replies, not even the documented append_notify Timeout — and once two of three nodes park the cluster stops deciding; witnessed at event_capacity 8, 64 and the shipped default 1024 (receipts ff4511e8, 76557a28, bbff5b4c), with the earlier harness transport jam retained as an excluded cause; limits: client-side trigger with no documented drain obligation, a dropped receiver unblocks the actor, and how many nodes a schedule parks is not bounded. (2) The core Sequence Paxos has no timer-driven repair for a lost Accepted reply: in the 2-node case where that one message is exactly what the quorum still needs, the entry stays undecided for 100 resend periods with only heartbeats after the drop, while the control decides in one step and a later proposal repairs it (receipt 092538c6); limit: only the 2-node configuration was probed. (3) append_notify can resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that was never decided there, shadowing the Superseded heuristic, and the scope is measured rather than argued: an unadopted entry yields a false Ok while an adopted entry yields a truthful Ok (receipt 78c53df3, which also records the takeover state); limits: both interleavings constructed, the Ok semantics a contract reading, and only a 2-second tick cadence probed. No necessary work remains unfinished within the run's limits.
